source_regions.S2.p2: Let O(n):=\{O\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}:O^{\top}O=I_{n}\} denote the real orthogonal group, equipped with Haar probability measure. It has two components, \{\det O=+1\}, \{\det O=-1\}, and each have Haar probability 1/2. For b\in\{-1,+1\}, we write \mu_{n,b} for Haar probability measure conditioned on \det O=b.
source_regions.S3.SS1.p1: Fix \kappa\geq 4. Let 3\leq n\leq d be the block dimension and k:=\lfloor d/n\rfloor the number of blocks. In the proof of the main theorem, we choose n=2T+1, where T is the algorithm’s query budget. This choice applies when T\geq 1 and 2T+1\leq d. The remaining cases are treated separately. For O\in O(n), define A_{O}:=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I_{n}-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^{\top}). (4) For \bm{O}=(O_{1},\ldots,O_{k})\in O(n)^{k}, set A_{\bm{O}}:=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(A_{O_{1}},\ldots,A_{O_{k}},I_{d-kn}\bigr). (5)
source_regions.S3.SS1.p2: For each b\in\{-1,+1\}, draw O_{1},\ldots,O_{k} independently from \mu_{n,b}, and let \mathcal{D}_{b} denote the law of A_{\bm{O}}. Thus the orthogonal matrices share the same determinant sign.
source_regions.S3.SS1.p3: Writing P_{b}:=\mathbb{E}_{O\sim\mu_{n,b}}[N(0,A_{O}^{-1})] for the single-block target mixture, the averaged target under \mathcal{D}_{b} is \bar{\pi}_{b}:=\mathbb{E}_{A\sim\mathcal{D}_{b}}[\pi_{A}]=P_{b}^{\otimes k}\otimes N(0,I_{d-kn}). (6) When kn=d, the identity block and the final Gaussian factor are omitted.
source_regions.A2.SS2.p2: We first separate the single-block mixtures using a bounded radial test, and then amplify this separation across independent blocks. The single-block argument combines a cancellation identity for Gaussian normalization factors with two spherical Poisson identities. Throughout this section, n\geq 3, \kappa\geq 4, and O is Haar distributed on the full orthogonal group O(n). Write U:=O_{11}, let p_{O} be the density of N(0,A_{O}^{-1}), and let p_{b} be the density of P_{b}, for b\in\{-1,+1\}.
source_regions.A2.SS2.SSS2.p3: For \lambda\geq 0, let h_{\lambda}(x):=e^{-\lambda\|x\|^{2}} and define H(\lambda):=\mathbb{E}\left[\det(O)\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}h_{\lambda}(x)p_{O}(x)\,dx\right]. Since the two determinant components have Haar probability 1/2, H(\lambda)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathbb{E}_{P_{+1}}h_{\lambda}-\mathbb{E}_{P_{-1}}h_{\lambda}\right). As 0<h_{\lambda}\leq 1, it follows that \operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})\geq 2|H(\lambda)|. (20) We compute H(\lambda) and then choose \lambda>0.

theorem actual_mixture_expectation_gap {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) :
    let μ := orthogonalHaar n
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
    let t : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x => Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2)
    let f : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ := fun O => ∫ x, t x ∂γ O
    Integrable t (νpos.bind γ) ∧ Integrable t (νneg.bind γ) ∧
      Integrable f νpos ∧ Integrable f νneg ∧
      (∫ x, t x ∂νpos.bind γ) = (∫ O, f O ∂νpos) ∧
      (∫ x, t x ∂νneg.bind γ) = (∫ O, f O ∂νneg) ∧
      ((∫ x, t x ∂νpos.bind γ) - (∫ x, t x ∂νneg.bind γ)) =
        2 * (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * f O ∂μ)
